display_title: 18-3-1 寻找混凝土的替代材料

sentences.en: Concrete is everywhere, but it’s bad for the planet, generating large amounts of carbon dioxide — alternatives are being developed
sentences.zh: 混凝土无处不在，但会产生大量二氧化碳，对地球环境不利。目前人们正着手开发替代材料。

sentences.en: Concrete is the second most used substance in the global economy, after water — and one of the world’s biggest single sources of greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 在全球经济中，混凝土是使用量仅次于水的物质，也是世界上温室气体排放量最大的单一来源之一。

sentences.en: The chemical process by which cement, the key ingredient of concrete, is created results in large quantities of carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 水泥是混凝土的关键成分，制造水泥的化学过程会产生大量二氧化碳。

sentences.en: The UN estimates that there will be 9.8 billion people living on the planet by mid-century.
sentences.zh: 联合国估计，到本世纪中叶，地球人口将达到98亿。

sentences.en: They will need somewhere to live.
sentences.zh: 这些人都需要有地方住。

sentences.en: If concrete is the only answer to the construction of new cities, then carbon emissions will soar, aggravating global warming.
sentences.zh: 如果建设新城市只能使用混凝土，碳排放量就会猛增，使全球变暖加剧。

sentences.en: And so scientists have started innovating with other materials, in a scramble for alternatives to a universal commodity that has underpinned our modern life for many years.
sentences.zh: 因此，科学家开始尝试利用其他材料进行创新，争相为这种多年来一直支撑着现代生活、几乎无处不用的商品寻找替代品。

sentences.en: The problem with replacing concrete is that it is so very good at what it does.
sentences.zh: 取代混凝土之所以困难，恰恰是因为它十分胜任现有的用途。

sentences.en: Chris Cheeseman, an engineering professor at Imperial College London, says the key thing to consider is the extent to which concrete is used around the world, and is likely to continue to be used.
sentences.zh: 伦敦帝国理工学院工程学教授克里斯·奇斯曼说，关键在于考虑混凝土在全世界的使用范围有多广，以及将来它可能还会在多大范围内继续使用。

sentences.en: ‘Concrete is not a high-carbon product.
sentences.zh: “混凝土并不是一种高碳产品。

sentences.en: Cement is high carbon, but concrete is not.
sentences.zh: 水泥是高碳的，但混凝土不是。

sentences.en: But it is the scale on which it is used that makes it high carbon.
sentences.zh: 然而，正是混凝土庞大的使用规模，使它的总碳排放居高不下。

sentences.en: The sheer scale of manufacture is so huge, that is the issue.’
sentences.zh: 光是生产规模就大得惊人，问题就在这里。”

sentences.en: Not only are the ingredients of concrete relatively cheap and found in abundance in most places around the globe, the stuff itself has marvellous properties: Portland cement, the vital component of concrete, is mouldable and pourable, but quickly sets hard.
sentences.zh: 混凝土的原料相对便宜，在世界多数地方都很丰富，混凝土本身也有出色的性能。其关键成分波特兰水泥既可塑形，也可浇注，却能迅速凝结变硬。

sentences.en: Cheeseman also notes another advantage: concrete and steel have similar thermal expansion properties, so steel can be used to reinforce concrete, making it far stronger and more flexible as a building material than it could be on its own.
sentences.zh: 奇斯曼还指出另一个优点：混凝土和钢材的热膨胀特性相近，因此可以用钢材加固混凝土，使它作为建筑材料时，比单独使用混凝土既坚固得多，又更具柔韧性。

sentences.en: According to Cheeseman, all these factors together make concrete hard to beat.
sentences.zh: 奇斯曼认为，所有这些因素加在一起，使混凝土很难被超越。

sentences.en: ‘Concrete is amazing stuff.
sentences.zh: “混凝土是种了不起的材料。

sentences.en: Making anything with similar properties is going to be very difficult.’
sentences.zh: 要制造出性能相近的材料，会非常困难。”

sentences.en: A possible alternative to concrete is wood.
sentences.zh: 木材是可能取代混凝土的一种材料。

sentences.en: Making buildings from wood may seem like a rather medieval idea, but climate change is driving architects to turn to treated timber as a possible resource.
sentences.zh: 用木材造楼或许颇有几分中世纪的味道，但气候变化正促使建筑师转而考虑使用经过处理的木材。

sentences.en: Recent years have seen the emergence of tall buildings constructed almost entirely from timber.
sentences.zh: 近些年，高层建筑中已出现几乎完全由木材建成的楼房。

sentences.en: Vancouver, Vienna and Brumunddal in Norway are all home to constructed tall, wooden buildings.
sentences.zh: 温哥华、维也纳和挪威的布鲁蒙达尔都已建起了高层木结构建筑。

sentences.en: Using wood to construct buildings, however, is not straightforward.
sentences.zh: 不过，用木材造楼并非易事。

sentences.en: Wood expands as it absorbs moisture from the air and is susceptible to pests, not to mention fire.
sentences.zh: 木材吸收空气中的水分时会膨胀，也易受虫害，更不用说火灾了。

sentences.en: But treating wood and combining it with other materials can improve its properties.
sentences.zh: 不过，对木材进行处理，并将其与其他材料结合，可以改善它的性能。

sentences.en: Cross-laminated timber is engineered wood.
sentences.zh: 正交胶合木是一种工程木材。

sentences.en: An adhesive is used to stick layers of solid-sawn timber together, crosswise, to form building blocks.
sentences.zh: 生产时，用胶黏剂把多层锯切实木交错粘合，制成建筑构件。

sentences.en: This material is light but has the strength of concrete and steel.
sentences.zh: 这种材料很轻，却具有混凝土和钢材的强度。

sentences.en: Construction experts say that wooden buildings can be constructed at a greater speed than ones of concrete and steel and the process, it seems, is quieter.
sentences.zh: 建筑专家说，木结构建筑的施工速度能比混凝土和钢结构建筑更快，而且施工过程似乎也更安静。

sentences.en: Stora Enso is Europe’s biggest supplier of cross-laminated timber, and its vice-president Markus Mannström reports that the company is seeing increasing demand globally for building in wood, with climate change concerns the key driver.
sentences.zh: 斯道拉恩索是欧洲最大的正交胶合木供应商。其副总裁马库斯·曼斯特伦表示，公司看到，全球对用木材建造房屋的需求在增加，主要推动因素是人们对气候变化的担忧。

sentences.en: Finland, with its large forests, where Stora Enso is based, has been leading the way, but the company is seeing a rise in demand for its timber products across the world, including in Asia.
sentences.zh: 斯道拉恩索总部所在的芬兰森林广袤，一直走在前列；不过，该公司还看到，包括亚洲在内，世界各地对其木材产品的需求都在增长。

sentences.en: Of course, using timber in a building also locks away the carbon that it absorbed as it grew.
sentences.zh: 当然，将木材用于建筑，还可以把树木生长时吸收的碳封存起来。

sentences.en: But even treated wood has its limitations and only when a wider range of construction projects has been proven in practice will it be possible to see wood as a real alternative to concrete in constructing tall buildings.
sentences.zh: 但即使是处理过的木材也有局限。只有在更广泛的建设项目中经过实践验证，才有可能把木材视为建造高层建筑时真正可以取代混凝土的材料。

sentences.en: Fly ash and slag from iron ore are possible alternatives to cement in a concrete mix.
sentences.zh: 在混凝土拌合料中，粉煤灰和冶炼铁矿石产生的炉渣都有可能替代水泥。

sentences.en: Fly ash, a byproduct of coal-burning power plants, can be incorporated into concrete mixes to make up as much as 15 to 30% of the cement, without harming the strength or durability of the resulting mix.
sentences.zh: 粉煤灰是燃煤发电厂的副产物。将其加入混凝土拌合料，可以替代配方中多达15%至30%的水泥，同时不影响成品的强度或耐久性。

sentences.en: Iron-ore slag, a byproduct of the iron-ore smelting process, can be used in a similar way.
sentences.zh: 冶炼铁矿石产生的炉渣也是一种副产物，可以按类似的方式使用。

sentences.en: Their incorporation into concrete mixes has the potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 把这两种材料掺入混凝土，有望减少温室气体排放。

sentences.en: But Anna Surgenor, of the UK’s Green Building Council, notes that although these waste products can save carbon in the concrete mix, their use is not always straightforward.
sentences.zh: 不过，英国绿色建筑委员会的安娜·瑟杰纳指出，尽管使用这些废料能减少混凝土拌合料的碳排放，实际应用起来却未必简单。

sentences.en: ‘It’s possible to replace the cement content in concrete with waste products to lower the overall carbon impact.
sentences.zh: “可以用废料替换混凝土中的水泥，以降低整体碳影响。

sentences.en: But there are several calculations that need to be considered across the entire life cycle of the building — these include factoring in where these materials are being shipped from.
sentences.zh: 但必须按照建筑的整个生命周期进行几项核算，其中包括把这些材料的运输起点考虑在内。

sentences.en: If they are transported over long distances, using fossil fuels, the use of alternative materials might not make sense from an overall carbon reduction perspective.’
sentences.zh: 如果用化石燃料把这些材料长途运来，那么从整体减碳的角度看，采用替代材料或许就没有意义了。”

sentences.en: While these technologies are all promising ideas, they are either unproven or based on materials that are not abundant.
sentences.zh: 这些技术构想都很有前景，但它们要么还未经验证，要么依赖并不充裕的材料。

sentences.en: In their overview of innovation in the concrete industry, Felix Preston and Johanna Lehne of the UK’s Royal Institute of International Affairs reached the conclusion that, ‘Some novel cements have been discussed for more than a decade within the research community, without breaking through.
sentences.zh: 英国皇家国际事务研究所的菲利克斯·普雷斯顿和约翰娜·莱内在概述混凝土行业的创新时得出结论：“研究界对某些新型水泥的讨论已持续十多年，却一直没有取得突破。

sentences.en: At present, these alternatives are rarely as cost-effective as conventional cement, and they face raw-material shortages and resistance from customers.’
sentences.zh: 目前，这些替代品的成本效益很少能与传统水泥相当，而且还面临原材料短缺和客户抵触的问题。”
